title: Runtime fidelity planner and per-layer accuracy budget enforcement for mixed-precision dispatch
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a runtime 'fidelity planner' that enforces per-layer accuracy budgets and dynamically selects among FP16 / FP8 / INT8 kernels during inference. The planner should consult calibration profiles, live confidence telemetry, and per-model accuracy budgets to choose the highest-efficiency kernel that satisfies an accuracy guardrail. This ticket covers the runtime policy, a lightweight in-flight validation harness, rollout controls (canary + gradual gating), and telemetry required to measure delta in downstream eval prompts.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime fidelity planner can select different kernel implementations for the same operator at runtime based on per-layer budget and telemetry.
Planner consults persisted calibration profiles (FP8/INT8) and rejects kernels whose expected accuracy loss exceeds budget for a given layer.
In-flight validation harness runs shadow-execs on a sampled subset and reports accuracy deltas to the eval dashboard without impacting production latency SLA.
Canary rollout path exists: we can enable mixed-precision kernel choices for a customer route with a percent-based rollout and automatic rollback if accuracy regressions exceed thresholds.
Telemetry is emitted: per-layer chosen dtype, expected vs observed accuracy delta, confidence score, fallback events, and cost-per-token delta.
Unit and integration tests cover planner decision logic and safety fallbacks for new kernel types (FP8/INT8).
Documentation updated: design doc, runtime API flags, and operation runbook for investigating fidelity incidents.
No customer-facing errors or increased 95th percentile latency in canary beyond specified SLOs during rollout tests.
notes: Motivation: existing static model tags (quant profiles) are insufficient for workloads with variable token distributions — we need per-layer, per-inference decisions that respect an overall accuracy budget.

Strategy: implement a planner loop that evaluates candidate kernels in order of cost-efficiency (INT8 -> FP8 -> FP16) but gates each selection with expected accuracy loss computed from calibration artifacts and recent shadow validation samples.
Accuracy budgeting: budgets expressed as per-layer allowable BLEU/ROUGE/LLR delta or a unified loss-increase percent. Budgets are stored with model metadata and editable from console.

Shadow validation: run a sampled duplicate of payloads through candidate kernel path asynchronously; compare outputs using fast heuristics (logit distance, token match rate) to estimate drift. Only a tiny percentage of requests are shadowed to control cost.
Safety: explicit hard-fallback to FP16 or previous stable variant on any mismatch or confidence threshold breach. Fallbacks must be immediate and instrumented.
Telemetry schema: see links to telemetry proto and dashboard (below).
comments: 2026-02-21 — Aisha Patel: Spike completed. Microbench shows INT8 kernels can reduce per-token cost by ~2.3x on Llama-variant encoder layers with <0.6% downstream metric delta for narrow prompt sets. Draft design pushed to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/RT-FIDELITY-SPK.

2026-02-28 — Marco Chen: Prototype planner implemented in runtime branch feature/fidelity-planner. Basic decision logic and calibration lookup working. Shadow validation harness integrated with sampling path. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9124.

2026-03-04 — Sofia Nguyen (ML Eval): Ran eval suite across 12 prompt families. Observed a few failure modes on noisy prompts where INT8 causes >1.5% LLR regression on hallucination-sensitive tasks. We need stricter per-layer budgets for attention and feedforward layers in decoders.

2026-03-07 — Marco Chen: Added per-operator profile weights and slack margin config. Running longer integration test against canary traffic (internal). Observed shadow sampling overhead within acceptable CPU budget. Next: add automatic rollback hook and dashboard charts.

2026-03-10 — Security team: Reviewed telemetry for PII risk; no payload data stored, only hash-based fingerprints and metric aggregates. Recommend adding periodic retention audits. Marking for follow-up in security backlog.
